page: Vultr vcg-a16-3c-32g-8vram is a Cloud GPU instance featuring 3 dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. For accelerated workloads, it includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU, delivering 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 170 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scored 1705.53, and the Geekbench single-core score reached 1343.0. However, multi-core performance is limited, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 5059.76 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3293.0, both falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 35.06 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 26.33 GB/sec. Large language model inference using a medium 7B model yields a text generation speed of 4.56 tokens per second.

This instance offers an entry-level tier for GPU-accelerated computing by utilizing a fractional GPU allocation, which provides resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that do not require a full dedicated GPU. Given the hardware profile, this server is suited for light GPU-accelerated tasks, basic image processing, text processing, and development environments. It is less suited for heavy multi-threaded CPU tasks, high-throughput database operations, or large-scale LLM inference due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth performance.
